abstract: Responses to targeted and immune checkpoint therapies in metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) are heterogeneous, and no predictive biomarker is available. We performed a meta-analysis of DNA methylation profiles from 727 ccRCC tumors, benchmarked four published signatures, and identified a hyper-methylated subtype (15% of tumors) associated with shorter overall survival. Integration of 589 matched transcriptomes showed that hyper-methylated tumors were more proliferative, depleted in endothelial tip cells, and overexpressed DNMT3B while underexpressing TET2. We then developed a gene expression classifier based on nine gene ratios that predicted methylation subtypes in an independent cohort (AUC-ROC = 0.96). In four treated cohorts, predicted hyper-methylated tumors had shorter progression-free survival on sunitinib but not on immune checkpoint-based regimens. Hyper-methylated primary tumors responded better to atezolizumab plus bevacizumab than to sunitinib, whereas hypo-methylated metastases benefited more from sunitinib. Methylation subtypes may thus help guide treatment selection in metastatic ccRCC.
